Pairwise environmental differences from site-level covariates

Source: R/mlpe_covariates.R
pairwise_endpoint_covariates.Rd

Constructs pairwise environmental-mismatch covariates from site-level values. The result can be used alongside isolation-by-resistance (IBR) terms to model isolation by environment (IBE) within mlpe_covariates or wishart_covariates.

Usage

pairwise_endpoint_covariates(
  x,
  coords = NULL,
  transform = c("absdiff", "sqdiff", "euclidean", "manhattan"),
  scale = FALSE
)

Arguments

x

Site-level covariates. Supported inputs:

  • A numeric vector (one covariate per site).

  • A numeric matrix or data frame (sites in rows, covariates in columns).

  • A terra::SpatRaster: values are extracted at coords.

coords

Required when x is a raster. Focal-point coordinates in the same projection as x; accepts the same inputs as conductance_surface.

transform

How to collapse site-level values into a pairwise environmental-mismatch measure.

"absdiff"

Absolute difference between endpoints: \(|x_i - x_j|\). One output column per covariate. Symmetric; suitable when the hypothesis concerns an association between environmental dissimilarity and differentiation, regardless of direction.

"sqdiff"

Squared difference: \((x_i - x_j)^2\). One output column per covariate. Like "absdiff" but penalizes large differences more heavily.

"euclidean"

Euclidean distance across all covariates: \(\sqrt{\sum_k (x_{ik} - x_{jk})^2}\). Collapses multivariate data to a single dissimilarity measure.

"manhattan"

Manhattan (city-block) distance: \(\sum_k |x_{ik} - x_{jk}|\). Collapses to a single measure; less sensitive to outliers than Euclidean.

scale

Logical. If TRUE, standardize (z-score) site-level covariates before computing the pairwise transform. Recommended when covariates are on different scales.

Value

A numeric matrix of class "terradish_pairwise_covariates" with one row per unordered site pair and named columns reflecting the chosen transform (e.g. "absdiff_altitude", "euclidean").

Details

The function produces a \(n(n-1)/2 \times p\) matrix of pairwise endpoint-difference covariates, where \(n\) is the number of focal sites and \(p\) is the number of output columns (one per input covariate for "absdiff" and "sqdiff"; one for "euclidean" and "manhattan"). Rows correspond to the lower triangle of the pairwise distance matrix, scanned column by column.

The returned object has class "terradish_pairwise_covariates". This class carries the original site-level covariate matrix and the chosen transform as attributes, so that terradish_cv_folds can automatically rebuild the correct pairwise covariates for each train/test split.

If x already has class "terradish_pairwise_covariates", it is returned unchanged (pass-through).

Interpreting pairwise effects

Construct one pairwise_covariates object to use the same environmental transforms and geographic distances in both likelihood families. Their fitted conductance surfaces are conditional on these terms, and conductance signs can change when the mean structure changes. Report fits with and without pairwise effects. A uniform ~ 1 conductance model with pairwise terms represents IBD plus IBE, not IBE alone.

A positive environmental coefficient means differentiation increases with environmental difference conditional on resistance. It does not distinguish assortative mating, dispersal filtering, local adaptation, or site variance that rises at environmental extremes. MLPE coefficients are unconstrained; Wishart kernel weights are nonnegative. Compare their effects in resistance-distance units with terradish_ibe_ratio, which divides by the resistance coefficient and propagates joint uncertainty. Ratios are undefined when that denominator is zero.

See also

pairwise_covariates, mlpe_covariates, wishart_covariates, terradish_cv_folds, terradish

Other measurement models: generalized_wishart(), leastsquares(), mlpe(), mlpe_covariates(), pairwise_covariates(), terradish_measurement_model, wishart_covariance(), wishart_covariates()

Examples

library(terra)

data(melip)
altitude <- terra::unwrap(melip.altitude)
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)

# Absolute altitude difference for every pair of sites, after
# standardizing the site values. One row per pair, in dist() order.
z_abs <- pairwise_endpoint_covariates(altitude, coords,
                                      transform = "absdiff", scale = TRUE)
head(z_abs)
#>      absdiff_spatial_template_lowres
#> [1,]                       0.5217511
#> [2,]                       1.6264202
#> [3,]                       0.6761406
#> [4,]                       0.1773603
#> [5,]                       1.1508445
#> [6,]                       0.4351686

# Several site-level columns collapsed into one Euclidean difference.
site_env <- data.frame(
  altitude = scale(as.numeric(terra::extract(altitude, coords)[, 2])),
  xcoord = scale(terra::geom(coords)[, "x"])
)
z_env <- pairwise_endpoint_covariates(site_env, transform = "euclidean")
head(z_env)
#>      euclidean
#> [1,] 0.5218581
#> [2,] 2.6250996
#> [3,] 1.5786658
#> [4,] 1.4060711
#> [5,] 1.1508931
#> [6,] 0.4478144
